correctness.rationale: Reflection characterization (including degenerate axes) and uniform morphic doubling are proved without finite extrapolation. Published exact factor complexity and period-doubling palindromic-periodicity counts, algebraically compared over all remainder ranges, exclude every odd part >=9. Explicit full small-factor sets show 1/3/5 positive and 7 negative; independent verifier corroborates both predicate implementations, morphism and factor counts.

evidence: Fici–Shallit–Simpson (2025), Theorem 13, gives counts for palindromic periodicities, a strict superset of palindrome pairs.
Their count equals ordinary factor complexity at odd part 7, so their result does not entail the failure of universal palindrome-pair symmetry in that family.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The relevant stronger *membership* set is the palindromic-periodicity language. Its exhaustive count rules out odd parts outside 1,3,5,7, but does not settle the odd-part-7 boundary. The exact substitution reflection criterion plus a length-seven obstruction resolves the gap; hence the published broader count does not subsume this statement.

evidence: The 2015 source sets the general question and obtains results for other families.
The 2025 theorem supplies f(n) and the ordinary-factor formula supplies q(n), with equality exactly at odd parts 1,3,5,7; the new counterexample removes 7.
Closest semantic results concern string attractors in period-doubling and automorphism properties of related lifts, not palindrome-pair factor-length spectra.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Compared logical implications: a count for the superclass implies failure only when it is smaller than factor complexity, whereas equality does not imply pair membership. The missing implication at odd part 7 is settled by exhibiting a non-reflection-invariant factor and establishing exact even-length desubstitution. No examined published claim dominates this classification.

originality.rationale: The 2015 natural universal palindrome-pair problem and the 2025 exact counts of the broader palindromic-periodicity class do not determine the odd-part-7 boundary, which is demonstrably different. The new desubstitution equivalence and explicit 7-obstruction close the implication gap. No equivalent claim found in examined primary sources and searched research records. Unindexed older results remain a risk.

value.rationale: This is the exact all-length solution to an established universal-palindrome-pair question in a classical automatic sequence. The exceptional odd-part-7 family separates a stronger property from the known weaker palindromic-periodicity counts and gives an infinite structural classification rather than a finite arithmetic extension.
